name: acad-viewports
description: Paperspace viewport control: creation (rectangular and polygonal), scale, lock, shade plot, and the per-viewport layer overrides that let one model serve an architectural plan, a fire plan and a furniture plan from the same geometry.
intent_examples: hide layers in this viewport only
make a viewport on the layout
rotate coordinates in this viewport only

zsynchronizuj skale rzutni ze skala adnotacyjna

tools_summary.name: clip_viewport_by_object
tools_summary.description: Clip a viewport to an existing closed shape - a closed polyline, circle or ellipse already in paper space. Use this when create_polygonal_viewport's vertex list is the wrong tool because the outline already exists, for instance a site boundary traced earlier. The shape must be closed; an open polyline is refused rather than assigned and left to corrupt the viewport later.

tools_summary.name: create_polygonal_viewport
tools_summary.description: Create a non-rectangular paperspace viewport from an ordered vertex list in paper-space coordinates. Needs at least 3 vertices; the outline is closed automatically. Use this for L-shaped or angled sheet windows.

tools_summary.name: create_viewport
tools_summary.description: Create a rectangular paperspace viewport on the named layout: a window width x height centred at 'center' in paper-space coordinates. Switches to that layout and back on its own, so it works from model space. Optional scale is the model-to-paper factor (0.02 = 1:50).

tools_summary.name: delete_viewport
tools_summary.description: Delete a paperspace viewport by handle. The model geometry it showed is untouched - only the window is removed.

tools_summary.name: get_viewport_extents_in_model
tools_summary.description: Return the model-space rectangle a viewport is currently showing, derived from its centre, paper size and scale. Use this to work out what geometry a sheet window actually covers before annotating it.

tools_summary.name: get_viewport_info
tools_summary.description: Full descriptor of one viewport by handle, including its frozen layers and which layers carry property overrides.

tools_summary.name: list_viewports
tools_summary.description: List paperspace viewports with handle, layout, paper geometry, scale, lock state and how many layer overrides each carries. Pass layoutName to restrict to one tab, omit it for the whole drawing. Read-only.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_annotation_scale
tools_summary.description: Set the annotation scale of a paperspace viewport, which decides what size annotative text and dimensions plot at in that window, and which annotative objects appear in it at all. By default the viewport's zoom scale is set to match, the way AutoCAD's own UI keeps the two linked; pass syncViewScale false to set annotation scale alone. The scale must already be in the drawing's list - use annotative.add_scale_to_list first if it is not.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_layer_freeze
tools_summary.description: Freeze layers in ONE viewport only. This is the mechanism that lets a single model produce an architectural plan and a fire plan: freeze the layers each sheet must not show, in that sheet's viewport, without touching the model or any other viewport.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_layer_thaw
tools_summary.description: Thaw layers that were frozen in one viewport, so they display there again. Layers not frozen in that viewport are left alone.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_lock
tools_summary.description: Lock or unlock a viewport. A locked viewport cannot have its zoom or scale changed by panning inside it, which is the single most common way an issued sheet silently ends up at the wrong scale.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_on_off
tools_summary.description: Turn a viewport's display on or off. An off viewport keeps its position, size and scale but renders nothing - useful for sheets under construction without deleting the window.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_scale
tools_summary.description: Set the model-to-paper scale of a viewport (0.02 = 1:50, 0.01 = 1:100, 0.001 = 1:1000). Locking the viewport afterwards is what stops an accidental zoom changing the drawn scale of an issued sheet.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_shade_plot
tools_summary.description: Set how a viewport plots: 'AsDisplayed', 'Wireframe', 'Hidden' or 'Rendered'. Hidden is what removes obscured 3D edges on a plotted sheet without changing the model.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_twist
tools_summary.description: Rotate the view inside a viewport by an angle, without rotating the model. Use it to put a wing of a building square on the sheet when it sits at an angle in the model - the drawing reads straight while the geometry stays where the survey put it.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_ucs
tools_summary.description: Give one paperspace viewport its own coordinate system, independent of the drawing's current UCS. This is what lets one sheet annotate a rotated wing of a building in that wing's own coordinates while the neighbouring viewport stays on the world axes. Pass a saved UCS name, or 'world' to clear it. Also sets UCSVP so the setting is stored with the viewport instead of vanishing at the next layout switch.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_view_direction
tools_summary.description: Set which way a viewport looks at the model: a named preset (top, bottom, front, back, left, right, sw-iso, se-iso, ne-iso, nw-iso) or an explicit direction vector. This is what turns one 3D model into a plan, an elevation and an isometric on the same sheet without duplicating geometry.

tools_summary.name: set_viewport_visual_style
tools_summary.description: Set the visual style a viewport displays and plots with - 2dWireframe, Hidden, Realistic, Conceptual, Shaded and whatever else the drawing defines. Unknown names are refused with the list of what this drawing actually has, since visual styles are per-drawing rather than fixed.

tools_summary.name: sync_viewport_to_annotation_scale
tools_summary.description: Set a viewport's zoom scale to match the annotation scale it already carries. set_viewport_annotation_scale does this by default; this tool is for repairing a viewport where the two have drifted apart - text sized for 1:50 on a window drawn at 1:100. Reports the scale before and after and whether anything changed.
